title: Why cities grow
paragraphs: A popular view holds that cities grow because jobs attract people. Economists studying nineteenth-century urban growth have complicated this picture. In several industrial regions, population rose first, driven by migrants fleeing agricultural decline, and employment expanded afterward as employers found a ready supply of labor. The evidence is not uniform, however, and some historians warn that records from the period are too patchy to settle the question. What can be said with confidence is that causation ran in both directions: jobs drew workers, and workers made new jobs viable.
